newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Transport Council takes first look at lorry pricing.
newsitem.headline: Transport Council takes first look at lorry pricing.

text.p: The Transport Council had a first attempt on Thursday at creating a pricing system for heavy goods lorries reflecting the scale of damage done by different vehicle types.

Talks centred on Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock's proposal to revise extend the EuroVignette lorry charging system, agreement on which remains "a long, long way" off even according to the Commissioner.

"It's not something which will be brought to a conclusion during the Irish presidency...nor possibly will it be concluded during the Dutch presidency," Council President Michael Lowry told a news conference.
There was scant detail of substance available on the day's other agenda items.

Ministers had their second meeting with their counterparts from the central and east European countries, this time sticking to a specific discussion on tariffs and the possibilities for common policies on rail and bimodal transport for the countries involved.
Another orientation debate took place on a draft regulation on the access conditions to EU road passenger markets for non-national transport companies.
The same applied for Commission proposal COM(96)190 to simplify procedures for international carriage of passengers by bus and coach, as currently defined by Regulation 684/92.
